<Rep. Jared Huffman>: H.R. 839 is an unnecessary attack on science-based conservation that would undermine voluntary, market-driven habitat protection in one of the most threatened ecosystems on the planet. This legislation fundamentally mischaracterizes the Muleshoe National Wildlife Refuge Land Protection Plan as federal overreach when it actually operates entirely through willing seller participation and expands rather than restricts private property rights.
The United States has already lost approximately 80% of its original grasslands, with the southern high plains losing half of their native grasslands to development.\1\ Muleshoe National Wildlife Refuge, established in 1935 as Texas's oldest national wildlife refuge, provides critical habitat for sandhill cranes, pronghorn, lesser prairie-chickens, and many declining grassland bird species. The Land Protection Plan would enhance habitat connectivity across a landscape essential for species survival and climate resilience.
\1\Moore, Calen. NPR in Kansas City. ``How fast food and big beef are helping High Plains ranchers save dwindling native grasslands''. (February 16, 2024).
H.R. 839 would block a completely voluntary process that works only with willing sellers and actually expands landowners' options by providing additional market opportunities for those who choose to participate. The legislation would interfere with private property rights by preventing landowners from voluntarily selling their land for conservation purposes or accessing North America Wetlands Conservation Act (NAWCA) funding, which leverages public and private investments to support local habitat conservation through collaborative partnerships.\2\
\2\North American Wetlands Conservation Act (NAWCA) U.S. standard grants: U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service. FWS.gov. Last visited on July 9, 2025.
Rather than representing a ``federal land grab,'' the Land Protection Plan follows established, transparent procedures under current National Wildlife Refuge laws. The expanded acquisition boundary simply defines where Fish and Wildlife Service can work with willing sellers over time--it doesn't mandate that all 700,000 acres will be acquired.\3\ FWS cannot and will not force any landowner to sell their property, making claims of federal overreach demonstrably false.
\3\United States Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) ``Land Protection Plan Report for Muleshoe National Wildlife Refuge'' (February 2023).
The legislation ignores the economic benefits that refuge expansion would bring to local communities.\4\ As noted by the FWS refuge manager, the plan would attract tourism, boost local economies, and increase county revenues.\5\ NAWCA grants create economic partnerships that benefit local communities while advancing conservation goals, demonstrating that conservation and economic development can work hand in hand.\6\
\4\Liu, H., Hou, L., Kang, N., Nan, Z., & Huang, J. (2022). The economic value of grassland ecosystem services: A global meta-analysis. Grassland Research, 1(1), 63-74. https://doi.org/10.1002/glr2.12012.
\5\Nations, R. (2024, September 10). Landowners to meet, discuss Muleshoe Wildlife Refuge Plan. Plainview. http://www.myplainview.com/ news/article/landowners-meet-discuss-muleshoe-wildlife-refuge- 19591630.php.
\6\North American Wetlands Conservation Act (NAWCA) U.S. standard grants: U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service. FWS.gov. Last visited on July 9, 2025.
H.R. 839 is part of a broader effort to dismantle federal conservation programs at a time when habitat loss and climate change are accelerating threats to wildlife.\7\ The bill would jeopardize essential habitat for vulnerable species and block proven conservation tools that respect private property rights while addressing the biodiversity crisis facing grassland ecosystems.
\7\American Stewards of Liberty. ``The Muleshoe Land Grab''. Last accessed on July 9, 2025.
Notably, this legislation appears to be moot following the United States Fish and Wildlife Service's July 30, 2025, withdrawal of the Muleshoe Land Protection Plan under President Trump's Executive Order 14154.\8\ The agency's decision to withdraw the plan demonstrates that H.R. 839 was always an unnecessary political exercise. By blocking voluntary conservation efforts that would benefit both wildlife and local economies, H.R. 839 and the UWFWS's withdrawal represents a missed opportunity to address the grassland habitat crisis through collaborative, market-based solutions that respect private property rights while advancing critical conservation goals.
\8\United States Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS). Press Release. ``USFWS Withdraws Land Protection Plan Expansion for Muleshoe National Wildlife Refuge''. July 30, 2025.
Jared Huffman,
Ranking Member.
